## Hurricane Helene Impact on Virginia Vegetation {.unnumbered .unlisted}

::: {.vvn-subtitle}
Storm Damage, Satellite Coverage, and Treatment-Counterfactual Analysis
:::

::: {.vvn-byline}
By **Yujuan Gao** · Visualizing Virginia's Numbers (VVN) · Virginia Tech · September 10, 2026
:::
:::

On September 26–27, 2024, Hurricane Helene made landfall and swept through western Virginia, delivering historic rainfall and catastrophic winds to Appalachian communities. This analysis uses Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 optical imagery from Google Earth Engine to quantify vegetation damage across 10 counties using a matched treatment–counterfactual design.

<details class="about-research">
<summary>About This Research</summary>
<div class="about-content">

### Background

Hurricane Helene made landfall in Florida on September 26, 2024, and tracked through the Appalachian region, bringing extreme rainfall and flooding to southwest Virginia. Satellite monitoring enables rapid, county-level damage assessment without ground surveys.

### Data & Methods

| Item | Details |
|------|---------|
| **Source** | Sentinel-2 SR Harmonized, Sentinel-1 GRD (ESA/Copernicus) |
| **Geography** | 10 counties in southwest Virginia |
| **Period** | June 2024 – March 2025 |
| **Processing** | Google Earth Engine |
| **Index** | NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index) |

### Limitations

- Simulated data used for demonstration
- County-level aggregation may mask sub-county variation
- NDVI measures greenness, not structural damage

</div>
</details>

## Storm Track Through Virginia {.finding}

::: {.finding-statement}
Hurricane Helene crossed Virginia as a Category 1 storm on September 27, delivering 10–20 inches of rain to mountain communities.
:::

## Treatment and Counterfactual Sites {.finding}

::: {.finding-statement}
Ten treatment sites in the storm path were matched to counterfactual sites based on elevation, slope, and land cover.
:::

Each treatment site (orange) is linked to 10 counterfactual matches (blue) that share similar terrain but were outside the storm's direct path. Click any marker to see site details.

## Vegetation Greenness Dropped After the Storm {.finding}

::: {.finding-statement}
All 10 counties showed NDVI declines of 0.19–0.28 between August and October 2024.
:::

NDVI values dropped from a pre-storm range of 0.67–0.75 down to 0.39–0.55 after the hurricane. Patrick County experienced the largest absolute drop, while Craig County showed the smallest.

```{r fig-03}
#| fig-cap: "NDVI comparison across 10 southwest Virginia counties before and after Hurricane Helene. Source: Sentinel-2 SR Harmonized, Google Earth Engine."
#| fig-alt: "Grouped bar chart showing NDVI values for 10 Virginia counties. Pre-storm values range from 0.67 to 0.75; post-storm values range from 0.39 to 0.55."
knitr::include_graphics("figures/01_ndvi_comparison.png")
```

---

## Conclusion {.unnumbered}

Hurricane Helene caused significant, measurable vegetation loss across southwest Virginia. Satellite monitoring — particularly SAR for cloud-free coverage — enabled rapid county-level damage assessment. The treatment–counterfactual design confirms that the storm, not seasonal change, was the primary driver. Future work should examine recovery trajectories over 6–12 months.
